title: A dependency-gated option list clears the field's stored value on mount, before the user touches anything
body:
Filed unassigned per Prime Directive #10, found while wiring the detail page's inline editor to `FieldEditWidget` (#4220). Adjacent to that card but **not** in it: this fires on the FORM path too, and the right behaviour is a judgement call rather than an obvious bug fix.

## What happens

The four fixed-option widgets (`SelectField`, `MultiSelectField`, `CheckboxesField`, `RadioField`) end their cascade resolution with a "drop what is no longer offered" effect, keyed on `[options, gated]`:

```
useEffect(() => {
  if (readonly) return;
  if (selected.length === 0) return;
  const stillOffered = selected.filter((v) => options.some((o) => o.value === v));
  if (stillOffered.length !== selected.length) onChange(stillOffered);
}, [options, gated]);
```

`resolveCascadingOptions` (`packages/core/src/evaluator/optionRules.ts`) returns an **empty** `options` whenever the list is gated:

```
const gated = dependsOnFields.length > 0 && isOptionGroupGated(dependsOn, record);
const options = gated ? [] : resolveVisibleOptions(rawOptions, record, scope);
```

So while a field is waiting on its controlling field, `options` is `[]`, nothing the field holds is "still offered", and the effect writes the field empty — **on mount, with no interaction**. The widget is simultaneously rendering `OptionsEmptyState` ("Select Country first"), i.e. it is telling the user it cannot offer anything, while deleting what they had.

## Measured on `origin/main` @ `5e2e9fa8c`

A `multiselect` declaring `dependsOn: ['country']` with per-option `visibleWhen`, mounted with `dependentValues: {}` (controlling field empty) and a stored value of `['zj']`:

```
multiselect-empty-province   rendered (the "select the parent first" hint)
onChange calls               [ [ [] ] ]        ← one call, with an empty array
```

The single `SelectField` behaves the same way with `undefined` instead of `[]`. Both fire before any user interaction.

## Why this is a judgement call, not an obvious fix

Two readings, and they disagree:

- **"Gated means unknown"** — while the parent is empty the widget has no information about which stored values are valid, so it should display the hint and leave the value alone. The user has not made a decision; the widget is making one for them, destructively.
- **"Gated means invalid"** — a value whose parent is unset is inconsistent data by definition, and ADR-0058 clearing it is the system converging the record.

The second reading is defensible on a form the user is actively filling in. It is much harder to defend on **mount**, where the record simply arrives from the server with the parent empty (a later-cleared parent, an import, a partially-migrated row) and the widget silently stages a deletion the user never asked for and cannot see.

## Reachability

The form renderer forwards `dependentValues`, so any record whose controlling field is empty while the dependent picklist has a value hits this on render. The detail page's inline editor reaches it too since #4220 (it renders every editable field of a section at once, and each `onChange` goes straight into the record draft the save bar commits).

## Not the same as #2968

#2968 (closed, PR #2969) is a `select` losing its value to a `''` written by a different path, and its own analysis explicitly rules the cascade clear out — those fields had no `dependsOn`, so `gated` was false. This is the `dependsOn` path, which that card never reached.

## Related work already landed

#4220 guards the neighbouring case only: the effect no longer prunes when the field declares **no `options` at all** (nothing was ever configured, so there is nothing to prune against). A gated field HAS an authored list, so it is untouched by that guard and still clears. The four `rawOptions.length === 0` guards in `packages/fields/src/widgets/` are where a decision here would land.
